title: Buying clothes
context: You are in a clothes shop.

choices.text: Yes, I'm looking for a blue shirt.

choices.feedback: Too short. Use a full sentence.
Polite, but you asked for help later, so be clear.
Try: "I think I am a medium."

choices.text: Can I try it on, please?

choices.feedback: Blunt. Ask about price politely instead.

title: At a restaurant
context: You arrive at a restaurant with a friend.

n1.speaker: Waiter
n1.say: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?

choices.text: No, but a table for two, please.

n2.speaker: Waiter
n2.say: Here is the menu. Are you ready to order?

choices.text: Yes, I'd like the chicken soup, please.
Not yet, could we have a few more minutes?
choices.feedback: Good way to ask for time.

n3.speaker: Waiter
n3.say: Would you like anything to drink?

end.speaker: Waiter
end.say: Perfect. I will bring it soon.

title: Airport check-in
context: You are at the airline check-in desk.

n1.speaker: Agent
n1.say: Good morning. May I see your passport and ticket?

choices.feedback: Hand the documents over and say "Here you are."

n2.speaker: Agent
n2.say: Would you like a window or an aisle seat?

choices.text: A window seat, please, if possible.

n3.speaker: Agent
n3.say: Do you have any bags to check in?

end.speaker: Agent
end.say: Here is your boarding pass. Gate 12, boarding at ten.

title: Hotel check-in
context: You arrive at a hotel late in the evening.

n1.speaker: Receptionist
n1.say: Welcome. Do you have a booking with us?

n2.speaker: Receptionist
n2.say: How many nights are you staying?

n3.speaker: Receptionist
n3.say: Breakfast is from seven to ten. Anything else?

choices.text: Could you tell me the Wi-Fi password, please?

title: Asking for directions
context: You are lost in a city centre.

n1.speaker: Passer-by
n1.say: Hi, you look lost. Can I help?

choices.text: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
Yes, please. Where is the station?

n2.speaker: Passer-by
n2.say: Go straight, then turn left at the bank.

choices.text: Sorry, could you say that again, please?
choices.feedback: Great way to ask for repetition.

n3.speaker: Passer-by
n3.say: It is about ten minutes on foot.

choices.text: Thank you so much for your help!

end.speaker: Passer-by
end.say: You are welcome. Have a good day!

title: A phone call to book an appointment
context: You call a clinic to make an appointment.

n1.speaker: Receptionist
n1.say: Good morning, City Clinic. How can I help you?

choices.text: Hello, I'd like to make an appointment, please.
Hi, can I book an appointment?

n2.speaker: Receptionist
n2.say: Is Tuesday at ten o'clock OK for you?

choices.text: Tuesday at ten is fine, thank you.
Do you have anything later in the day?

n3.speaker: Receptionist
n3.say: Could I have your name and phone number?

choices.text: Yes, it's Amina Ali, and my number is 555-0142.

choices.feedback: Give your full name and number.

end.speaker: Receptionist
end.say: Thank you. You are booked in.

title: Joining a team meeting
context: You join a weekly project meeting.

n1.speaker: Manager
n1.say: Let's start. Can you give us a quick update on your tasks?

choices.text: Sure. I finished the report and I'm now working on the slides.

n2.speaker: Manager
n2.say: Is there anything blocking your progress?

choices.text: I need access to the sales data. Could you help with that?
choices.feedback: Names the problem and asks for help.

choices.text: Yes, but it is your fault.

n3.speaker: Manager
n3.say: The deadline moved to Friday. Is that realistic?

choices.text: I think so, but I'll confirm by tomorrow.

choices.feedback: Good, but only if you are sure.

end.speaker: Manager
end.say: Great. Thanks, everyone. Let's finish here.

title: Handling a customer complaint
context: A customer is unhappy with a late delivery. You work in customer service.

n1.speaker: Customer
n1.say: My order is two weeks late. This is unacceptable!

choices.text: I'm very sorry about the delay. Let me check your order right away.
Of course. I can refund you, or send a replacement. Which would you prefer?
I'll ask my manager and call you back today.
choices.feedback: Acceptable, but offer what you can do now.

n3.speaker: Customer
n3.say: How long will the refund take?

choices.text: It usually takes three to five working days.

choices.feedback: Find out or say you will.

end.speaker: Customer
end.say: Thank you for sorting this out.

title: Talking to a professor
context: You visit your professor during office hours about your essay.

n1.speaker: Professor
n1.say: Come in. What can I do for you?

choices.text: Thank you for seeing me. I'd like some feedback on my essay outline.
I have a question about the essay.

n2.speaker: Professor
n2.say: Your argument is clear, but you need stronger evidence.

choices.text: That's helpful. Could you suggest where I might find better sources?
choices.feedback: Shows you can act on feedback.

choices.text: I disagree. My evidence is fine.

n3.speaker: Professor
n3.say: Please send me a revised version by next week.

choices.text: Certainly. I'll email it to you by Monday.

end.speaker: Professor
end.say: Good. I look forward to reading it.

title: Interview: strengths and weaknesses
context: You are in the second stage of a management job interview.

n1.speaker: Interviewer
n1.say: What would you say is your greatest strength?

choices.text: I'm good at turning complex problems into clear plans that teams can follow.
I used to take on too much myself, so I've learnt to delegate and set priorities.

choices.feedback: A common cliché; be more original.

n3.speaker: Interviewer
n3.say: Where do you see yourself in five years?

choices.text: I'd like to lead a larger team and keep developing strategically.

end.speaker: Interviewer
end.say: Thank you. It was a pleasure to meet you.

title: Meeting someone new at a party
context: You meet a new person at a friend's party.

n1.speaker: New friend
n1.say: Hi, I'm Sara. I don't think we've met.

choices.text: Hi Sara, I'm Omar. Nice to meet you.

n2.speaker: New friend
n2.say: How do you know the host?

choices.text: We work together. How about you?

n3.speaker: New friend
n3.say: What do you do in your free time?

choices.text: I enjoy football and cooking. What about you?

end.speaker: New friend
end.say: It was great talking to you.

title: Opening a bank account
context: You visit a bank to open an account.

n1.speaker: Bank clerk
n1.say: Welcome. How can I help you today?

choices.text: I'd like to open a current account, please.
Can you tell me about your accounts?

n2.speaker: Bank clerk
n2.say: Do you have a form of identification?

choices.text: Yes, I have my passport and a proof of address.

choices.feedback: Honest; ask what else is needed.

n3.speaker: Bank clerk
n3.say: Would you like online banking as well?

choices.text: Yes, please. How do I set it up?

end.speaker: Bank clerk
end.say: Your account will be ready in a few minutes.

title: Questions after a presentation
context: You have just finished a business presentation and the audience asks questions.

n1.speaker: Audience member
n1.say: Thank you. Could you explain how you calculated those figures?

choices.text: Certainly. We based them on last year's sales, adjusted for expected growth.
Good question. I can walk you through the method.
That's a fair concern. We've prepared a conservative scenario as well.
I'm not sure, I'll check and follow up.

n3.speaker: Audience member
n3.say: Thank you. That was very helpful.

choices.text: Thank you for your questions. Please feel free to email me.

choices.feedback: Add an invitation to follow up.

title: At the doctor's
context: You are visiting a doctor because you feel unwell.

n1.speaker: Doctor
n1.say: Hello. What seems to be the problem?

choices.text: I've had a sore throat and a headache since Monday.
Yes, it was thirty-eight degrees this morning.

choices.feedback: Say "I am not sure; I did not check."

n3.speaker: Doctor
n3.say: I will give you a prescription. Take one tablet twice a day.

choices.text: Thank you. Should I take it with food?

end.speaker: Doctor
end.say: Rest well and drink plenty of water.
